ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Direction-aware latent tokens trained from posed renders alone
PROPOSAL: Train a transformer encoder that reads 12 posed renders of an object and writes 512 latent tokens. A decoder takes a 3D point and a viewing direction and returns density and color, so highlights can move with the camera. Supervision is the rendering loss only, so no watertight meshes and no distance-field conversion are needed. Use 20000 Objaverse objects at 256 pixels and test on 500 held-out objects.
CONTROLS: Compare chamfer distance with a signed-distance autoencoder of equal latent size, and compare PSNR and LPIPS with the same decoder when the viewing direction input is zeroed. Ablate the token count at 128 and 512.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: Chamfer stays within 5 percent of the geometry-only autoencoder while PSNR on glossy objects improves by roughly 1.5 dB. Failure case: thin structures blur when 512 tokens cannot hold fine detail.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Posed-render latent autoencoder with view-dependent decoding on a pooled corpus
PROPOSAL: Train a 24-layer transformer encoder that reads 16 posed renders of an object and writes 512 latent tokens. A decoder takes a 3D point and a viewing direction and returns density and color. Supervision is the rendering loss only, with 3 seeds. Draw 20000 objects from Objaverse, ShapeNet and Google Scanned Objects, render them at 512 pixels, and test on 500 held-out objects, scoring PSNR and chamfer distance at the last checkpoint and at earlier ones.
CONTROLS: Compare chamfer distance with a signed-distance autoencoder of equal latent size and with a variant whose decoder drops the viewing direction. Ablate encoder depth and decoder width, scoring both on PSNR and LPIPS.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: Expect PSNR near 31 dB on held-out objects and chamfer distance close to the geometry-only autoencoder. The decoder may fail on translucent objects, where density and color trade off against each other.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Image-conditioned flow sampler for object latents with matching shape and gloss
PROPOSAL: Freeze the latent autoencoder and train a 400M-parameter rectified-flow transformer that samples latent tokens given DINOv2 features of a rendered input view. Train on 100000 Objaverse objects with randomized lighting so the input image carries material cues. Decode each sample and render it from the input camera and from 8 novel cameras. Report mask IoU, PSNR and LPIPS at the input view, and CLIP similarity on novel views.
CONTROLS: Compare with a two-stage sparse-voxel generator and with a variant whose autoencoder color is averaged over views. Ablate the conditioning, using CLIP features instead of DINOv2 features, and drop the lighting randomization.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Input-view PSNR rises by about 2 dB over the view-averaged variant on glossy objects, and mask IoU stays above 0.9. The sampler could fail when the input lighting differs from the training lights, producing flat color.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Silhouette agreement of generated latents with the input viewpoint at higher capacity
PROPOSAL: Freeze the latent autoencoder and train a 1.3B-parameter rectified-flow transformer that samples latent tokens given CLIP features of a rendered input view. Train on 100000 Objaverse objects, then draw 3 samples for 2000 test images from Google Scanned Objects and Objaverse. Measure mask IoU and depth error at the input camera, training with 5 seeds and reporting the spread.
CONTROLS: Compare with a two-stage sparse-voxel generator trained on the same data and with a flow model of 400M parameters. Ablate the conditioning features, trying DINOv2 and CLIP, and the guidance weight.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Mask IoU should reach 0.92 at the input camera, with depth error below the two-stage generator. It could fail if the 2000 images are dominated by simple objects so that differences vanish in the average.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Does a direction-conditioned color head cost geometry accuracy in a small autoencoder
PROPOSAL: Train two small latent autoencoders on 3000 Objaverse objects at 128 pixels with 256 latent tokens. The first decodes density only, supervised by depth renders. The second adds a color head conditioned on viewing direction, supervised by color renders. Both use the same optimizer and schedule, with 3 seeds. Compare surface recovery by chamfer distance and F-score at 0.01 on 300 held-out objects.
CONTROLS: Compare against a color head that ignores viewing direction, to separate color supervision from direction. Vary the weight on color loss at 3 values. Use a signed-distance autoencoder of matching latent size as a geometry-only reference.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Chamfer differs by less than 3 percent between the geometry-only and color models, with the direction-aware head matching the view-independent one. Color gradients could distort thin parts, which would show in F-score first.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Geometry accuracy of a color-decoding latent autoencoder on a mixed corpus
PROPOSAL: Train a color-decoding latent autoencoder with 512 latent tokens on 30000 objects from Objaverse and ShapeNet at 256 pixels, with 5 seeds. Supervise density with depth renders and color with renders conditioned on viewing direction. Compare surface recovery by chamfer distance and F-score at 0.01 on 300 held-out objects, tracking both at 6 intermediate checkpoints.
CONTROLS: Compare against a depth-only autoencoder of matching latent size and a signed-distance autoencoder fitted on watertight ShapeNet meshes. Vary the weight on color loss.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Geometry error should plateau by the third checkpoint and sit within 3 percent of the depth-only model. A failure would be color supervision pulling surfaces outward on reflective objects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Joint training of the autoencoder and generator with relit renders
PROPOSAL: Train the latent autoencoder on 200000 Objaverse objects rendered under random environment maps at 256 pixels, then train a flow transformer on its latents given a DINOv2 embedding of one rendered view. Decode generated latents and render them under the input lighting. Evaluate on the reflective subset of a 1000-object test split, with LPIPS and PSNR at the input view and CLIP similarity on novel views.
CONTROLS: Compare with the same pipeline trained on unlit renders, and with a two-stage voxel generator. Ablate the environment-map augmentation and the conditioning embedding.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Relit training should cut LPIPS at the input view by about 10 percent on reflective objects relative to unlit training. It could fail when environment maps are too few, leaving the generator unable to separate material from lighting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Autoencoder fidelity on glossy objects with a pooled pretraining corpus
PROPOSAL: Pretrain the latent autoencoder on 500000 objects pooled from Objaverse, ShapeNet, Google Scanned Objects and ABO, rendered at 512 pixels with 24 posed views, and train with 3 seeds. Test on the 1000 most reflective objects of a held-out split, scoring PSNR, LPIPS and chamfer distance. Report the same scores for latent sizes of 128, 256, 512 and 1024 tokens.
CONTROLS: Compare with a signed-distance autoencoder trained on the same corpus after mesh repair, and with a decoder that drops viewing direction. Ablate the rendering loss weight and the resolution used in training.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Highlight error should fall as tokens grow, flattening at 512 tokens, with chamfer near the signed-distance reference. The corpus mix could fail to help if few of its objects are reflective.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Three ways to encode direction-dependent color in a latent decoder
PROPOSAL: Train three decoders on top of one frozen encoder with 512 latent tokens: spherical harmonics coefficients of degree 3 per point, an MLP taking the viewing direction, and view-averaged color as a reference. Use 10000 Objaverse objects at 256 pixels. Score PSNR and LPIPS on novel views of 400 held-out objects, with separate scores for the glossy third of the set.
CONTROLS: Compare against the geometry-only decoder for chamfer distance, to confirm that adding color does not hurt shape. Ablate the harmonics degree at 1, 2 and 3, and the MLP width.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: The MLP should lead spherical harmonics by about 1 dB on glossy objects and tie on matte ones. Harmonics of low degree could fail to represent sharp highlights, which would show as blur.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Decoder comparison on color from viewing direction with extended data coverage
PROPOSAL: Train two decoders on top of one frozen encoder with 512 latent tokens: spherical harmonics coefficients per point and an MLP taking the viewing direction. Use 10000 objects from Objaverse, ShapeNet and ABO at 256 pixels, with 8 seeds each. Score PSNR and LPIPS on novel views of 400 held-out objects.
CONTROLS: Compare against the geometry-only decoder for chamfer distance, and against view-averaged color. Ablate the harmonics degree and the MLP width, scoring all variants on every seed.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Both decoders should land within 1 dB of each other, with the MLP ahead on glossy objects. Differences could fall inside seed noise, leaving no clear winner.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training from raw meshes without repair: geometry error check
PROPOSAL: Train the latent autoencoder directly on raw non-watertight meshes rendered at 256 pixels, using rendering loss only, on 5000 Objaverse objects with 512 latent tokens. Build a comparison arm by repairing the same meshes to watertight form and fitting signed distance targets. Score chamfer distance and F-score on 300 held-out objects.
CONTROLS: Compare against a signed-distance autoencoder on repaired meshes of the same objects, and against the autoencoder on raw meshes with depth supervision only. Ablate the number of training views.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Chamfer on raw meshes should land within 5 percent of the repaired pipeline while skipping conversion. It could fail on meshes with inverted faces, where renders disagree about the surface.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Preprocessing-free training measured against per-object field fitting
PROPOSAL: Train the latent autoencoder on raw meshes rendered at 256 pixels with rendering loss only, using 5000 Objaverse objects and 512 latent tokens. Build a comparison arm that fits a radiance field per object for 2000 of them to supply targets, plus a repaired-mesh arm for the same objects. Score chamfer distance and F-score on 300 held-out objects, with 3 seeds for each arm and PSNR from 12 views.
CONTROLS: Compare against a signed-distance autoencoder on repaired meshes, and against the same model trained on field-fitted targets. Ablate the number of views and the loss weight on color.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Raw-mesh training should match the field-fitted arm within 4 percent on chamfer. Thin parts could lose accuracy when meshes carry holes, visible in F-score.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: One-stage image-to-3D generation without coarse occupancy or canonical orientation
PROPOSAL: Train a flow transformer on 300000 Objaverse objects that maps noise to the full set of latent tokens in one stage, given DINOv2 features of a rendered view, with no coarse occupancy step. Objects are placed in the camera frame of the input, so no post-hoc alignment is applied. Test on 2000 images, scoring mask IoU, pose error against ground truth, PSNR at the input view and CLIP similarity.
CONTROLS: Compare with a two-stage sparse-voxel generator and with the same transformer trained on canonically oriented objects followed by alignment. Ablate the conditioning features and the number of latent tokens.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: Camera-frame generation should cut pose error by about 40 percent relative to the canonical-orientation arm, with comparable mask IoU. It could fail on symmetric objects where orientation is ambiguous.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Orientation handling of the generator measured on a 2B-parameter flow transformer
PROPOSAL: Train a 2B-parameter flow transformer on 300000 Objaverse objects that maps noise to latent tokens given CLIP features of a rendered view, in camera-frame orientation. Draw 3 samples for 2000 test images from Objaverse, ShapeNet and Google Scanned Objects. Score pose error against ground truth and mask IoU, with 5 seeds, and report both at 4 checkpoints during training.
CONTROLS: Compare with the same transformer trained on canonically oriented objects followed by alignment, and with a two-stage sparse-voxel generator. Ablate the conditioning features and the guidance weight.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: Pose error should fall to roughly half that of the aligned arm by the last checkpoint. Gains may vanish if the test images contain mostly upright objects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Do highlights move with the camera in generated objects
PROPOSAL: Train the latent autoencoder on 15000 Objaverse objects at 256 pixels with 512 latent tokens and a direction-conditioned decoder. Select 200 mirror-like and glossy test objects and render 24 viewpoints on a circle around each. Segment specular regions with a brightness threshold and track highlight position and intensity across views. Report the correlation with ground-truth renders and the error in specular regions.
CONTROLS: Compare against a decoder with view-averaged color and a decoder that conditions on direction only through the camera pose. Ablate the token count at 256 and 512, and check geometry with chamfer distance.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Highlight position correlation should reach 0.9 for the direction-conditioned decoder against 0.5 for view-averaged color. It could fail for objects with sharp edges, where highlights jump between views.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Specular region error with an extended data mixture and repeated training runs
PROPOSAL: Train the latent autoencoder on 15000 objects from Objaverse, ShapeNet and ABO at 256 pixels with 512 latent tokens and a direction-conditioned decoder, using 8 seeds. Select 200 mirror-like and glossy test objects and render 24 viewpoints. Report the error in specular regions defined by a brightness threshold, and PSNR on full images.
CONTROLS: Compare against a decoder with view-averaged color and a signed-distance autoencoder for geometry. Ablate the token count and the training resolution.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Specular-region error should drop by about a third relative to view-averaged color. Spread between seeds could be large enough to blur the comparison.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Latent size against memory: tokens versus voxel grids
PROPOSAL: Train the direction-conditioned autoencoder with 64, 128, 256 and 512 latent tokens on 25000 Objaverse objects at 256 pixels. Train a sparse-voxel latent autoencoder at 32 and 64 resolution on the same renders for the memory comparison. Record peak training memory, chamfer distance and PSNR on 500 held-out objects.
CONTROLS: Compare each latent design at matched memory and at matched quality, and against a signed-distance autoencoder for geometry. Ablate the decoder depth.
COST: 640
PREDICTION: Tokens should reach the voxel quality at 64 resolution with about a quarter of the memory. Fine geometry could fail to fit in 64 tokens, which would show as high chamfer.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Memory footprint of token latents against voxel latents at higher resolution
PROPOSAL: Train the direction-conditioned autoencoder with 128, 256 and 512 latent tokens on 25000 objects from Objaverse and ShapeNet at 256 pixels, with 3 seeds. Train a sparse-voxel latent autoencoder at 64 and 128 resolution on the same renders. Record peak training memory, chamfer distance and PSNR on 500 held-out objects, and the same figures after 5 stages of training.
CONTROLS: Compare both designs at matched memory and at matched quality, and against a signed-distance autoencoder for geometry. Ablate the decoder depth and the learning rate.
COST: 640
PREDICTION: The token design should match voxel quality at 64 resolution with a fraction of the memory. Voxels at 128 resolution may win on chamfer if memory is unrestricted.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Lighting sensitivity of a frozen image-to-3D generator
PROPOSAL: Take the trained image-conditioned generator without further training and evaluate it on 300 held-out objects, each rendered under 6 environment maps from the same camera. Generate an object from each image and render it at the input view and 8 novel views. Report PSNR and LPIPS at the input view, and the variance of generated geometry, measured by chamfer distance between samples from different lightings.
CONTROLS: Compare against the generator conditioned on view-averaged color and against a two-stage sparse-voxel baseline. Ablate the conditioning features using CLIP instead of DINOv2.
COST: 96
PREDICTION: Geometry variance across lightings should stay below 5 percent of object size, with input-view PSNR dropping by under 1 dB for unusual lights. Strong colored lights could fail by shifting shape estimates.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fine-tuning a generator on a broad mixture before measuring lighting effects
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune the image-conditioned generator for 20000 steps on 40000 objects from Objaverse, ShapeNet and ABO, then evaluate on 300 held-out objects rendered under 6 environment maps. Report PSNR and LPIPS at the input view, and chamfer distance between generated shapes under different lightings, using 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: Compare against the generator before fine-tuning and against a two-stage sparse-voxel baseline. Ablate the conditioning features and the learning rate used for fine-tuning.
COST: 96
PREDICTION: Fine-tuning should improve input-view PSNR by about 1 dB, with geometry variance across lightings staying small. Gains could vanish if the extra data is mostly matte.
